answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The lantern multiplier is published, charged in bridge, and summit lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 975 identities would post 2849 proofs and burn roughly 2 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
